subject: Livepage fanout: partial response delays & mitigation steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@pulsegrid.com>, ops@pulsegrid.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Livepage fanout: partial response delays & mitigation steps

Hi Alicia / PulseGrid ops team,

We're seeing a spike in partial-generation delays for requests routed through your livepage configuration (region: us-west-2). Some requests return shorter-than-expected chunks or delayed second-chunk streaming between ~08:50-09:05 PDT. We detected this as elevated p99s for multi-chunk streaming and increased requeue rates in the routing layer.

Immediate context:
- Affected surface: hosted-generation -> streaming responses for sessions using the livepage routing policy.
- Window observed: ~08:45-09:05 PDT (we're still analyzing residuals).
- Customer impact: intermittent elongated streaming tails and occasional truncated second chunk.

What we've done so far:
- Automatically routed new requests away from the affected fanout group to a healthy pool (reduction in new-hit error rate).
- Flushed a cached fanout topology hint causing suboptimal fanout for long sessions.
- Gathered candidate diagnostics (attached: diagnostic_log_20280817.txt).

Next steps from Redwood:
1) We're continuing to route traffic to fallback pools and will keep that routing in place until the full root cause is confirmed.
2) Ben and the runtime team are running an additional KV-coherency sweep and re-evaluating the fanout boundary heuristics.
3) We'll share a follow-up with a postmortem draft and recommended mitigations within the day.

Temporary ask for PulseGrid:
- If you can share any recent changes to your livepage configuration or client SDK flags in the last 24 hours, that will help correlate.

Apologies for the disruption — I'll keep this thread updated in real time.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Livepage fanout: partial response delays & mitigation steps

Marissa — quick technical status update for the thread and for PulseGrid when we share:

Root-cause hypothesis (working): a transient fanout topology hint became stale after an internal KV rebalancing complimented by a prefetch fanout expansion. For long-running streaming sessions, that produced a probe to a secondary shard that had delayed cache warmup leading to elongated tail behavior.

Actions taken (completed):
- Deployed a scoped routing rule to prefer warm shards for existing sessions (manual override for fanout affinity).
- Ran a KV coherence job to remove the stale hint and rehydrate local topology (this materially reduced requeue rates).
- Instrumented additional tracing on fanout boundary decisions and added an alert for fanout mismatch ratio >1.5% per minute.

Recommended customer-facing wording for the status update:
"Redwood detected elevated streaming latency for a subset of long-running sessions due to a transient fanout topology hint mismatch. We routed traffic away from affected fanout groups and rehydrated topology caches; normal behavior resumed in the fallback pool. Engineering is finalizing a post-incident mitigation to prevent recurrence."

Note on session affinity: the fallback pool preserves affinity for active sessions for 95% of cases. For strict affinity customers, we can coordinate a maintenance window to rebind affinity state if you prefer a no-fallback policy.

I'll attach the short diagnostics we used and a draft postmortem.

— Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: [Update] Livepage fanout incident — status page entry and postmortem draft

Hi Alicia — thank you for confirming. Quick update and next steps:

- Current status: We validated that fallback routing eliminated the majority of customer-visible delays by 09:20 PDT and have left fallback in place for stability.
- Impact summary: Partial streaming delays affected ~0.7% of multi-chunk streaming requests for PulseGrid between 08:45–09:05 PDT; no data loss was observed.
- Root cause (summary): transient fanout topology hint mismatch after an internal KV rebalance, combined with a prefetch fanout expansion affecting long-running sessions.
- Mitigations completed: routing override, KV coherence sweep, added tracing and alerting.

We've published a short status page entry (link below) and attached a postmortem draft for your review. We plan to incorporate any feedback and publish a final postmortem within 48 hours.

Status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2028-08-17-livepage-fanout
Postmortem (draft): attached (postmortem_draft_pulsegrid.docx)

If PulseGrid prefers we can schedule a 30-minute review with our runtime team tomorrow to walk the postmortem and planned fixes (fanout hint expiry adjustment and safer prefetch rollouts).

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
